def _get_bind_address(address: str) -> str:
    """Determine the actual address to bind to.

    When ``address`` is ``"0.0.0.0"`` (the default IPv4 wildcard), IPv6 is
    available on this system, and the user did not explicitly configure
    ``server.address``, we bind to ``"::"`` instead. Binding to the IPv6
    wildcard with ``IPV6_V6ONLY`` disabled accepts both IPv4 and IPv6 clients,
    enabling automatic dual-stack support on capable systems.

    If the user explicitly set ``server.address`` (including to ``"0.0.0.0"``
    or a specific IP), or IPv6 is not available, the original address is
    returned unchanged so that explicit configuration is always respected.

    Parameters
    ----------
    address
        The configured server address.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The address to actually bind to.
    """
    if (
        address == "0.0.0.0"  # noqa: S104
        and socket.has_ipv6
        and not config.is_manually_set("server.address")
    ):
        return "::"
    return address


def _bind_server_socket(
    server_address: str, bind_address: str, port: int, backlog: int
) -> tuple[socket.socket, str]:
    """Bind a server socket, falling back to the IPv4 address if needed.

    Attempts to bind to ``bind_address`` first (which may be the IPv6 wildcard
    ``"::"`` for dual-stack support). If that raises an ``OSError`` with errno
    ``EAFNOSUPPORT`` (address family not supported), binding falls back to
    ``server_address`` instead. Any other error (e.g. ``EADDRINUSE``) is
    re-raised without a fallback so that the caller can handle port retries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    server_address
        The originally configured server address, used as the fallback target.

    bind_address
        The preferred address to bind to.

    port
        The port number to bind to.

    backlog
        The maximum number of queued connections.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[socket.socket, str]
        The bound socket and the address it was actually bound to.
    """
    try:
        return _bind_socket(bind_address, port, backlog), bind_address
    except OSError as exc:
        if exc.errno == errno.EAFNOSUPPORT:
            # The system does not support the preferred address family (e.g. no
            # IPv6). Fall back to binding on the originally configured address.
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Address %s not supported, falling back to %s.",
                bind_address,
                server_address,
            )
            return _bind_socket(server_address, port, backlog), server_address
        raise
